text:
Maria Chen: Hey infra team — kicking off bring-up for a new GPU cluster in us-west3. Need a concise checklist for the GitOps/Helm deployment pipeline, image/artifact replication, and final handoff. Anyone who did this recently?

Jake Torres: I ran a similar flow for eu-west2. Key gotchas: chart repo access from the new VPC and stale images in the regional registry.

Li Wei: We switched to an OCI mirror (oras) + GCS backend rather than rsync. Steps we used: bootstrap control plane, install ArgoCD, then Argo apps for infra and apps. Brief snippet:```bash
# bootstrap k8s cluster
kubectl apply -f cluster-bootstrap.yaml
# install argocd
helm repo add argo https://argoproj.github.io/argo-helm
helm install argocd argo/argo-cd -n argocd --create-namespace
```

Sasha Patel: +1 on ArgoCD. Also remember to pre-create the service account used by the pipeline with these roles: compute.admin, container.admin, storage.admin, artifactregistry.writer. Without artifactregistry permissions the mirror job fails with 403.

Anita Gomez: Networking note: if we don't want egress, either set up VPC peering to central artifact registry or deploy a private Harbor in the region. NAT gateways are fine but costy for large pulls. For private deployments we used VPC peering + route advertisement.

Maria Chen: Good catch re cost. Any ballpark for the cost delta if we use NAT vs peered registry?

Jake Torres: NAT for 10TB/month egress would be ~ $700-$900 depending on provider. Harbor ops + infra ~ $300-400/month but adds management overhead. Mirrors reduce cross-region pulls.

Li Wei: For image sync we run a CI pipeline that iterates tags and uses `oras copy` to push to regional AR. Quick example:```bash
oras copy 
  docker://gcr.io/redwood-prod/model-server:sha-123 
  oci://us-west3-registry.redwood/artifacts/model-server:sha-123
```
Pipeline should report delta sizes. We also checksum layers to avoid double transferring.

deploy-bot: image-sync pipeline #1872 triggered for us-west3 by @Li Wei

deploy-bot: image-sync job completed: 146 images mirrored (8.1 GB total), 4 retries, duration 12m 33s.

Sasha Patel: Ops checklist for the cluster itself:
- GPU node pools: create separate nodepools for A100 vs H100, label nodes with `gpu-type`
- Install NVIDIA device plugin DaemonSet and GPU drivers (we use node-feature-discovery + driver installer)
- Install dcgm-exporter + prometheus scraping
- Configure taints/labels for spot vs guaranteed nodes
- Set pod disruption budgets for inference services

Anita Gomez: Validation steps before handoff:
1) `kubectl get nodes -L gpu-type` shows expected node counts
2) Run `nvidia-smi` in a test pod to confirm driver/GPUs visible
3) Pull sample images from regional registry from a node with `curl` (checks NAT/peering)
4) Confirm ArgoCD apps sync successfully and Helm hooks run
5) Run a small end-to-end inference job to validate latency and KV cache warmup

Maria Chen: Who can own the runbook PR? I'll draft the first pass with these notes and some commands. Can @Jake and @Sasha add the quota requests and firewall snippets?

Jake Torres: I can add quota commands and the provider-specific limit links. Also will add a template for GPU quota increase request:```text
Project: redwood-prod
Region: us-west3
Quota: NVIDIA A100 GPUs: 80
Justification: production inference capacity for X customers, traffic forecast...
```

Sasha Patel: I'll add firewall/NAT examples and the helm values for argocd + registry credentials secret formatting. Also recommend adding a step to validate KMS access for image decryption (if using envelope encryption).

Maria Chen: Awesome. I'll open the PR and tag @eng-infra for review. Once merged we can run the full pipeline and schedule a handoff runbook review w/ SRE. :thumbsup:
